reason: The text contains at least two named characters who are regular people: Moses (מֹשֶׁה), who is depicted as a shepherd tending flocks, and Jethro (יִתְרוֹ), identified as his father-in-law and priest of Midian. Both are presented as ordinary human beings engaged in mundane occupations before the divine encounter. While Moses becomes the focus of God's calling, at this point in the narrative he is portrayed as a regular person with a simple occupation.
